# Silas Bambil

<p class="role-line">Graduate student in Statistics<br>Georgia State University · Atlanta, Georgia</p>

<p class="lead">Understanding predictions under change.<br>Quantifying risk at the extremes.</p>

I am pursuing an MS in Mathematics with a concentration in Statistics at Georgia State University. I study how predictive models behave when conditions change, and how statistical methods help us understand rare, consequential losses.

## Selected research & software

::: {.feature-row}
::: {.feature-number}
01
:::
::: {}
<p class="meta">Research manuscript · 2026 · Unpublished</p>

### Reliable prediction under distribution shift

How do calibration, discrimination, and decision thresholds change when a model encounters a different population? This research compares model updating strategies using controlled simulations and a credit-risk benchmark.

[Explore the study →](research.qmd#distribution-shift)
:::
:::

::: {.feature-row}
::: {.feature-number}
02
:::
::: {}
<p class="meta">Independent research · 2026 · Unpublished</p>

### Stable fire-loss quantiles and far-tail uncertainty

An extreme-value analysis of approximately 1.25 million U.S. structure-fire loss records, examining the stability of extreme quantiles and the sensitivity of Expected Shortfall.

[Read about the fire-loss research →](research.qmd#fire-loss)
:::
:::

::: {.feature-row}
::: {.feature-number}
03
:::
::: {}
<p class="meta">Statistical software · R · In development</p>

### shiftadapt

An R package implementing logistic model updating and intervention selection under distribution shift, with separate data for fitting, selection, and final evaluation.

[View projects & software →](projects.qmd#shiftadapt)
:::
:::

## Teaching & learning

I support College Algebra students as a Graduate Lab Assistant at Georgia State University. Previously, I taught AP Calculus, AP Precalculus, and AP Statistics at Osceola School for the Arts.

[Teaching experience →](cv.qmd#teaching-experience)
:::

## Academic background

My training spans actuarial science, quantitative risk, and statistics. I hold an MS in Quantitative Risk Analysis and Management from Georgia State University and a BSc in Actuarial Science from KNUST.
